nodes: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: chronic metabolic disorder, insulin resistance, hyperglycaemia, HbA1c >6.5%, linked to obesity and cardiovascular risk.
Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF): EF <40%, dyspnoea, oedema, neurohormonal activation. Major cause of hospitalisation.
Hypertension: sustained systolic BP >130 mmHg, silent target-organ damage, major risk factor for stroke, myocardial infarction, and CKD.
Chronic Kidney Disease stage 3b: GFR 30-44, proteinuria, cardiorenal syndrome, accelerated cardiovascular risk.
Metformin: first-line T2DM drug, lowers hepatic glucose output, AMPK activation, weight-neutral, renal dose adjustment needed.
Empagliflozin: SGLT2-inhibitor, glucosuria, cardiorenal protection, FDA-approved for heart failure and CKD regardless of diabetes status.
Lisinopril: ACE inhibitor, reduces angiotensin II, lowers BP, first-line for HFrEF, reduces proteinuria in CKD.
SGLT2-inhibitor class: renal glucose excretion, natriuresis, cardiac preload/afterload reduction; benefit in CKD and HF independent of glycaemia.
Carvedilol: non-selective beta-blocker with alpha-1 blockade, reduces mortality in HFrEF, controls HR, mild antihypertensive effect.
Polyuria and polydipsia: hallmark osmotic symptoms of hyperglycaemia.
Headache and dizziness: common in uncontrolled hypertension.
Exertional dyspnoea and ankle oedema: cardinal symptoms of heart failure.
Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance: multi-disease symptom overlap seen in CKD anaemia, HF, and poorly controlled diabetes.

Finerenone (Kerendia): non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, reduces risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, and cardiovascular death in CKD with T2DM.

Patient/Physician Experience: Finerenone (DR6) shows high patient compliance and daily tolerability compared to older MRAs. Hyperkalemia vigilance requires baseline potassium monitoring (<5.0 mmol/L) and periodic follow-up.
Hyperkalemia (MRA-induced): elevation of serum potassium. DR6 carries a lower statistical risk of sudden potassium spikes than older steroidal MRAs.
